recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source work is needed unless FHIR-I later revises Event.recorded semantics or asks to align external Extension Pack wording beyond the already-published FHIR-46490 change.
issue_request: FHIR-39485 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I issue asking to clarify Event.recorded because "the record" was ambiguous when data is shared between systems. The approved resolution was to add comments explaining performing-practitioner record placement, patient or RelatedPerson disclosure, record transfers, delayed recording, resource.meta or Provenance, and repeated disclosures to different systems.
initial_application: Commits 99812c64733b4414b0ae7b7fabd148ce24a3330d and 868f2545ba0f1ab669a06a168942e5d858c7a3bc added and polished the Event.recorded comments in source/event/event-spreadsheet.xml, and merge e9cd0f5fbdc326197761a6c650f59796b57d7768 brought the branch into the main source history.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists event as an active logical pattern, so source/event/event-spreadsheet.xml is authoritative build-scope source. Generated/checked mapping-exception comparisons now include the clarified pattern comment. Later Immunization-specific recorded history, including FHIR-34301, did not supersede this Event pattern clarification, and the FHIR-34301 audit is already on the combined branch. The Extension Pack event-recorded extension was later clarified under FHIR-46490 outside this core checkout.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current Event.recorded comments already convey the required distinction between initial record capture/disclosure, record transfer, database-created timestamps, and Provenance/meta audit data.
